transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because of what's been going on at work. I drive at the warehouse, and the routing system there... it isn't just a normal computer to me anymore. I know it's been marking my moves. It's actually sending messages through our scanners to push me out, just because I'm one of the old hands. It's... it's just getting to be too much.
Alongside these beliefs about the routing system, have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, elated, or irritable?

Well, definitely not energetic. It's been more of the sad and hopeless side. When I was at my absolute lowest recently... I mean, I was barely eating, I stopped going to my choir practice, and I just felt like I had completely failed everybody. And the thing is, the whole time I felt like that, those scanner messages and... well, hearing the dispatch voices... they were happening right along with it. It all just kind of piled on at the exact same time.
Have you ever experienced these beliefs about the routing system or heard the dispatch voices during times when you were NOT feeling depressed or hopeless?

Yeah, actually. There was a stretch where my mood had eased up some. I wasn't feeling quite as low, and I was eating and talking a little more. But... even then, for a good few weeks, I still heard the dispatch calling my number. And I still knew the routing system was tracking me. So, the voices and the tracking, they didn't stop just because the sadness let up.
During that period when your mood had improved and you weren't feeling depressed, about how many weeks did the belief about being tracked and the dispatch voices continue on their own?

It was about three or four weeks, I'd say. Like I mentioned, my mood was definitely better... I was back to eating normal and talking to people a bit more. But the whole time, for those several weeks, I still kept hearing the dispatch calling out my number, and I still knew that routing system was tracking my every move.
Overall, how long have you been experiencing these beliefs about being tracked and hearing the dispatch voices, from when they first started until now?
Well, from the very beginning... I'd say the voices and, you know, the whole thing with the scanners tracking me... that's been going on for about a year and eight months now. It's been a while.

Over the entire year and eight months that you've had these beliefs and voices, roughly how much of that total time would you say you were also experiencing the depressed, hopeless mood you described?

Well, if I look back at the whole year and eight months... I'd say for most of that entire time, I've felt that heavy, depressed way. Even during the times when the fears about the warehouse routing system and the dispatch voices were a little quieter, I was still just... down. I felt completely empty. Most of this whole trouble, I haven't been able to get myself back into the things I used to do, like fishing or my woodworking. I haven't even been able to sit through family meals. So, yeah, the depression has been there for the vast majority of it.

latest_inference.note: Psychotic symptoms persisted for ~3-4 weeks without mood symptoms, confirming psychosis independent of mood episode, but depressive symptoms were present for the majority of the total illness duration (most of ~20 months). This pattern (mood symptoms present for majority of illness duration alongside independent psychotic periods) is characteristic of schizoaffective disorder and argues against schizophrenia, where mood episodes would need to be brief relative to the overall psychotic illness. F20.9 is therefore ruled out.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits concurrent psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions about being tracked by the routing system, auditory hallucinations of dispatch voices) and a major depressive episode (anhedonia, poor appetite, withdrawal from activities, feelings of failure) occurring simultaneously. Critically, there was a distinct 3-4 week period where psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) persisted in the clear absence of mood symptoms, satisfying the criterion for psychotic symptoms occurring without a major mood episode for at least 2 weeks. Additionally, mood symptoms (depressive type) have been present for the majority of the total 1 year 8 month illness duration, meeting the requirement that mood episodes be present for the majority of the total duration of illness. This combination—overlapping mood and psychotic symptoms, a discrete period of psychosis without mood disturbance, and predominance of depressive mood symptoms over the illness course—is diagnostic of Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (F25.1), rather than Schizophrenia (which would not require prominent mood episodes) or Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which would not have psychotic symptoms persisting independently of mood episodes for weeks).
